title: The attack surface includes pages the current product no longer links to, still holding their old trust model
index_line: T-0060 · SQL_EXEC · a legacy ASP page still concatenates SQL after the product moved on · php/asp/any-legacy-tree · corroborated
invariant_violated: A codebase is treated as the code the product uses. Every rewrite leaves files behind that nothing links to — and nothing authenticates, nothing reviews and nothing patches them either. A page from two product generations ago keeps the trust model it was written under, and stays reachable at its old URL because the server still serves the directory.

mechanism.does: the attacker enumerates legacy paths (old .asp/.php entry points) that the current UI no longer links to
the server resolves the path to an orphaned script still present in the web root
the legacy handler reads its parameters with the parsing conventions of its generation, which validate nothing
the script builds a database query by concatenating that parameter, as was normal when it was written
the query reaches the database parser and the attacker syntax executes
the result comes back, or is inferred from verbose error and timing differences

source.http.request.value: a parameter on an orphaned page — the page is not in any link graph, so it is found by enumeration or by source disclosure

sink.sql.concat.value: the legacy query string built by concatenation

encoding.string.value: quote-breaking payloads for the DB dialect in use

oracle.error.value: the legacy page usually has verbose errors enabled, which is the extraction channel

preconditions.expr: the server still serves the directory containing pre-rewrite scripts

check.spec: for p in /admin/ /legacy/ /old/ /includes/; do curl -sk -o /dev/null -w "$p %{http_code}\n" https://HOST$p; done

preconditions.expr: an orphaned script concatenates a request parameter into SQL
the orphaned path is not referenced by the current application

spec.method: grep the current UI and routes for the filename; zero references plus a 200 response is the proof

success: a script that no current page links to answers 200 and processes parameters
the response is verbose: a SQL error naming the dialect, or a result set that should be behind a login
removing the parameter changes the error, proving the parameter reaches the query
failure_like: the legacy directory is blocked at the server, or the old files were removed in the rewrite
false_positive: a 200 returning a generic error page — check whether the parameter influenced it
a legacy path served by the SPA fallback (200 with the app's HTML) — that is not the old script running

hazards: the audit unit is the deployed file list, not the repository: diff what the server serves against what the app references
rewrites leave includes, admin tools, installers and test harnesses behind; each is a time capsule of the old security posture
verbose errors are the norm in that vintage, which makes extraction cheap
related to T-0061 (a CGI multiplexer exposing every script): both are 'forgotten code is still reachable', but here the discovery is by path and there by a dispatcher parameter
non_transfers: deployments that ship only referenced files, or block unlinked directories
frameworks that route every request through a single front controller

provenance.author: Intezer research on XE Group zero-days (CVE-2024-57968 / CVE-2025-25181)
provenance.corroborates: the XE Group's use of the VeraCore upload validation and SQL injection flaws, including the 2020-era legacy page

provenance.author: Solis Security (independent analysis of the XE Group campaign)
provenance.corroborates: independent threat-research record of the same exploitation
